correctness.rationale: For n>=3 and 0<=t<=n the deleted-matching graph is connected. The Gravner–Lyu–Sivakoff 3-colour irrotationality criterion identifies synchronizing CCA and GHM initial states with integer 1-Lipschitz potential lifts, unique up to a global shift. Fix the left-shore potential minimum at zero and its range to 0,1,2; for each such left word, the permitted integer heights on a right vertex are the intersection of [A_i-1,A_i+1] over its remaining neighbours. Counting full, missing-one and extremal cases yields exactly 3[4^n+2*3^n-2^(n+2)+1+t*2^(n+1)+t(t-1)]. Both the t=0 and t=n boundaries are connected and included. Direct *independent* height enumeration agrees for all n=3..6 and t=0..n; independently running actual CCA and GHM dynamics until repetition for all 3^(2n) starts at n=3,4 verifies identical synchronization counts for each t. These finite tests corroborate but do not replace the all-n Lipschitz enumeration.

value.rationale: The number of synchronizing initial colorings is a natural basin-size invariant for two classical deterministic excitation rules. The complete matching-deletion family reveals a rigorously quantified pair interaction, second finite difference 6, not an arbitrary finite parameter slice: arbitrary t from 0 to n changes the graph connectivity pattern while preserving the winding criterion. It can be used to compare robustness to structured edge deletion and is not just a numerical experiment.
